    "document_title": "Jevlike ADAM Kaine harvest 2026-09-16 — handoff",
    "text": "- `TinyScorer` averages byte embeddings for option text without option positional embeddings. Consequently, byte permutations with the same retained byte counts have identical option representations. It is unsuitable as-is when argument order or identifier structure distinguishes actions. Context has positional embeddings but no contextual text encoder in this tiny path. - `FrozenTransformerScorer.forward` invokes its frozen encoder twice: once for context, once for the flattened batch of options. It then runs the shared attention head. “One pass” describes non-autoregressive decision scoring, not literally one encoder invocation or constant cost as the option list grows. This qualifies the earlier conversational shorthand. - [Text training](upstream/jevlike/train.py) uses ordinary supervised cross-entropy and AdamW, choosing by validation loss. It is not an RLCD implementation. Each row has one chosen label; several valid actions and abstention need an explicit data/objective treatment. - Default text limits are 192 context tokens and 32 option tokens; in the tiny path these are bytes. A software-action representation needs truncation checks that preserve discriminating evidence. - [Evaluation](upstream/jevlike/eval.py) reports top-1, top-3, ten-bin ECE, and a batch-rolled context control. ECE is measurement, not calibration training.",

    "text": "The encoder must accept both CPU buffers and GPU buffer handles:\n\n```rust\n/// A frame ready for encoding. Can be CPU pixels or a GPU buffer handle.\nenum FrameSource<'a> {\n    /// CPU-accessible pixel data (from PixmanRenderer / ExportMem)\n    Cpu {\n        data: &'a [u8],\n        width: u32,\n        height: u32,\n        stride: u32,\n        format: PixelFormat,\n    },\n\n/// GPU buffer handle (from GlesRenderer / DRM)\n    /// Encoder can import this directly without CPU copy\n    DmaBuf {\n        fd: OwnedFd,\n        width: u32,\n        height: u32,\n        stride: u32,\n        format: DrmFourcc,\n        modifier: DrmModifier,\n    },\n}\n```\n\nA CPU-based encoder (zstd diff, software x264) processes `FrameSource::Cpu`.\nA hardware encoder (VAAPI, NVENC) prefers `FrameSource::DmaBuf` (zero-copy) but can also accept `FrameSource::Cpu` (upload first, slower).",

    "document_title": "ADR 096 rev2 (amended) — Step-Level Rewards from Engine Replay, Structural vs VSA Judging, and Recurrent Depth for Axis-A (2026-08-15)",
    "text": "6. **The positional-encoding ablation runs before any architecture change.** `TinyTransformer` uses a **learned absolute position embedding** over a `max_seq_len` table (`crates/grug-train/src/transformer.rs:290, 310`). Depth-5/6 traces are longer than anything trained, so their position rows sit at initialisation — a mechanically sufficient cause of `trace_valid = 0.000` that was not previously on the Phase 51 risk list. NoPE beats every explicit scheme on downstream length generalization at zero extra cost ([2305.19466](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19466)); randomized PE adds +12.0% across 6000 models / 15 algorithmic tasks by removing the OOD-index failure ([2305.16843](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16843)); position coupling by structural role gives 6.67× length extrapolation and maps onto our step-indexed ADR-092 grammar ([2405.20671](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20671)). Kohli et al. hit the same split, using APE for 2-hop and switching to NoPE for depth extrapolation.",

    "text": "/// Encode a message to a length-prefixed byte vector.\npub fn encode<T: Serialize>(msg: &T) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CodecError> {\n    let payload = postcard::to_allocvec(msg)?;\n    let len = (payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes();\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(4 + payload.len());\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&len);\n    buf.extend_from_slice(&payload);\n    Ok(buf)\n}\n\n/// Decode a message from a byte slice (payload only, after length prefix).\npub fn decode<T: DeserializeOwned>(data: &[u8]) -> Result<T, CodecError> {\n    Ok(postcard::from_bytes(data)?)\n}\n\n/// Read a length prefix from a byte slice, returning (length, remaining).\npub fn read_length_prefix(data: &[u8]) -> Option<(u32, &[u8])> {\n    if data.len() < 4 { return None; }\n    let len = u32::from_le_bytes([data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3]]);\n    Some((len, &data[4..]))\n}\n```\n\nDefine `CodecError` wrapping postcard errors.\n\n- [ ] **Step 4: Update lib.rs**\n\n```rust\npub mod messages;\npub mod codec;\npub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: u32 = 1;\n```\n\n- [ ] **Step 5: Write tests**\n\nTest round-trip serialization for each message type. Test the codec encode/decode cycle. Test edge cases (empty regions, max values).",
